chief_complaint: Uncontrolled hypertension with metabolic syndrome (obesity, prediabetes) and recurrent urinary tract infections
history_of_present_illness: The patient is a 49‑year‑old woman with a long‑standing history of essential hypertension (diagnosed 2007) that remains poorly controlled (BP 150/98 mmHg). She has obesity (BMI ≥30 documented since 2010) and prediabetes (A1c 6.1% since 1999) without pharmacologic glucose‑lowering therapy. Chronic anemia has been present since 2007 and is being treated with vitamin B12 injections, suggesting a possible B12‑deficiency component. She experiences recurrent urinary tract infections dating back to 1995, most recently noted as an active problem. Since early 2019 she has increased alcohol consumption and has lost multiple teeth, reflecting ongoing oral health issues. Social determinants include chronic social isolation, unsatisfactory housing, and full‑time employment, which may impede adherence to lifestyle modifications. Overall, the clinical picture reflects multiple inter‑related cardiovascular, metabolic, renal, hematologic, and psychosocial risk factors with limited pharmacologic management.
past_medical_history: Resolved oral conditions include gingival disease, infection of tooth, and gingivitis (all resolved February 2019). Prior psychosocial stressors and limited social contact were documented as resolved in 2017 and 2019. No other chronic resolved conditions are noted.

active_medications.name: Vitamin B12 5 MG/ML Injectable Solution
active_medications.purpose: Management of anemia likely due to B12 deficiency

social_determinants: Patient reports chronic social isolation, unsatisfactory housing, full‑time employment, and high school education level. These factors may limit access to healthy foods, regular medical follow‑up, and adherence to lifestyle interventions.

Organ systems at elevated risk: cardiovascular (hypertension, obesity, prediabetes, alcohol use), renal (hypertension, recurrent UTIs, unknown eGFR), metabolic (obesity, prediabetes), hematologic (anemia), oral health (tooth loss), psychosocial (social isolation, housing instability).
